pois.name: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building
pois.description: Twin-towered civic skyscraper (243 m, 1991) by Kenzo Tange. The free observation deck on floor 45 is open until 23h — Tokyo's best free panorama, with Shinjuku, Fuji and Tokyo Bay visible on clear days.

pois.name: Kabukicho
pois.description: Tokyo's most intense entertainment and nightlife district: cinema towers, izakayas, host clubs, karaoke buildings, and a Godzilla head on the Toho Cinemas building. The Tokyu Kabukicho Tower (2023, 192 m) anchors the new Kabukicho Square redevelopment.

pois.name: Shinjuku Gyoen
pois.description: 58-hectare national garden blending French formal, English landscape and Japanese traditional styles. Tokyo's premier hanami spot in late March — over 1,100 cherry trees of 65 varieties. Once an imperial retreat until 1949.

pois.name: Omoide Yokocho
pois.description: Memory Lane — a narrow alley of tiny yakitori and kushiyaki bars dating from the post-WWII era. Smoke, skewers and Sapporo beer under lanterns, steps from the station's west exit.

pois.name: JR Shinjuku Station
pois.description: World's busiest railway station: 200 exits, 50 platforms, 3.5 million passengers per day across JR, Tokyo Metro and private lines. The South Exit terrace overlooks the station concourse.
